sentences.zh: 这些稻米种植园被认为是南方这一地区的粮仓。

sentences.en: So as they destroy crops and burn food stores, they are dealing a massive blow to the Confederacy.
sentences.zh: 因此，当他们摧毁庄稼和烧毁粮食储备时，他们正在给邦联以沉重打击。

sentences.en: But as all of this is happening, the other part of the operation begins.
sentences.zh: 但就在这一切发生的同时，行动的另一部分开始了。

sentences.en: Not only do they disembark soldiers, but they also send out rowboats.
sentences.zh: 他们不仅让士兵下船，还派出了划艇。

sentences.en: And those rowboats bring the freedom seekers back to the boats.
sentences.zh: 那些划艇将寻求自由的人们带回船上。

sentences.en: The black soldiers, fresh out of slavery themselves, begin to call out to the enslaved people working on the plantations.
sentences.zh: 这些刚从奴隶制中解放出来的黑人士兵，开始呼唤在种植园劳作的奴隶。

sentences.en: They walked up and down, waving flags, trying to attract the attention of the freedom seekers.
sentences.zh: 他们走来走去，挥舞着旗帜，试图引起寻求自由者的注意。

sentences.en: And one of the people watching in utter amazement as this unfolds is 88-year-old Rail Thin, Minus Hamilton.
sentences.zh: 而88岁的迈纳斯·汉密尔顿正惊奇地看着这一切发生。

sentences.en: He describes the enslaved people being in the rice fields hoeing rice when they first saw the Union gunboats coming up the river.
sentences.zh: 他描述说，当奴隶们第一次看到联邦炮艇沿河而上时，他们正在稻田里锄草。

sentences.en: And he talks about an overseer being in the rice fields with them on horseback.
sentences.zh: 他还提到监工当时正骑着马和他们一起在稻田里。

sentences.en: And so the overseer is seeing exactly what the enslaved people see.
sentences.zh: 所以监工看到的正是奴隶们所看到的。

sentences.en: And he is shouting to them that the Yankees have come and are going to sell them to Cuba.
sentences.zh: 他冲他们大喊，说北方佬来了，要把他们卖到古巴去。

sentences.en: And they should follow him to the woods and hide.
sentences.zh: 让他们跟着他躲进树林里。

sentences.en: And Minus Hamilton basically says, everybody went the other way.
sentences.zh: 而迈纳斯·汉密尔顿基本上说，大家都往另一个方向走了。

sentences.en: I was going to the boat.
sentences.zh: 我要去船那边。

sentences.en: Minus and his wife Hagar are both in the fields that day.
sentences.zh: 那天，迈纳斯和他的妻子哈加尔都在田里。

sentences.en: Together, they make their way to the gunboat, carrying nothing with them.
sentences.zh: 他们一起走向炮艇，什么也没带。

sentences.en: They really only had the clothing on their backs.
sentences.zh: 他们身上真的只有穿着的衣服。

sentences.en: He had a pair of pants and a shirt.
sentences.zh: 他只有一条裤子和一件衬衫。

sentences.en: And she only had just a single frock and a head tie.
sentences.zh: 而她只有一件单衣和一条头巾。

sentences.en: He laments that his two blankets, which are the only two things that he feels he can call his own,
sentences.zh: 他感叹说，他那两条毯子，是他觉得唯一属于自己的东西，

sentences.en: his two blankets are in the slave cabin and he has to leave them behind.
sentences.zh: 那两条毯子还在奴隶小屋里，他不得不把它们丢下。

sentences.en: But there is no time to waste.
sentences.zh: 但没有时间浪费了。

sentences.en: The freedom boat is here.
sentences.zh: 自由之船就在这里。

sentences.en: So as you can imagine, Minus Hamilton and his wife are elderly.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象，迈纳斯·汉密尔顿和他的妻子年纪都很大了。

sentences.en: He was likely one of the oldest people on these Cumbie rice plantations.
sentences.zh: 他很可能是这些康巴希稻米种植园里年纪最大的人之一。

sentences.en: So as they're moving to the boat, people are coming up behind them and telling them to hurry.
sentences.zh: 所以当他们走向船时，后面的人都在催促他们快点。

sentences.en: People are telling them that the Confederates are coming.
sentences.zh: 人们告诉他们邦联军队要来了。

sentences.en: To which Minus Hamilton's wife Hagar basically says, I'd like to see them try and stop us.
sentences.zh: 对此，迈纳斯·汉密尔顿的妻子哈加尔基本上说，我倒想看看他们怎么拦住我们。

sentences.en: She tells him to come on, right?
sentences.zh: 她叫他快点，对吧？

sentences.en: Come on, come plenty on.
sentences.zh: 快点，快点过来。

sentences.en: We're going to the boat.
sentences.zh: 我们要去船上了。

sentences.en: We're not worried about the Confederates here.
sentences.zh: 我们不担心这里的邦联军队。

sentences.en: The elderly couple are giddy.
sentences.zh: 这对老夫妇欣喜若狂。

sentences.en: Minus looks back and sees the plantation where he was held in bondage burn.
sentences.zh: 迈纳斯回头看着他曾被奴役的种植园燃烧。

sentences.en: Union Colonel Higginson, who later interviewed Minus, asked him how that moment felt.
sentences.zh: 后来采访迈纳斯的联邦希金森上校问他当时是什么感觉。

sentences.en: And Minus Hamilton laughs and says, Lord, Master, I didn't care nothing at all.
sentences.zh: 迈纳斯·汉密尔顿笑着说，上帝啊，主人，我一点都不在乎。

sentences.en: I was going to the boat.
sentences.zh: 我要去船上了。

sentences.en: You know, I and he is like, I'm not looking back.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我，他就像是说，我不会回头看。

sentences.en: I don't care.
sentences.zh: 我不在乎。

sentences.en: I'm leaving this all behind and I am going to freedom.
sentences.zh: 我把这一切都抛在身后，我要奔向自由。

sentences.en: But what Minus really remembered from that day were the black men in uniform.
sentences.zh: 但迈纳斯那天真正记住的是那些身穿制服的黑人男子。

sentences.en: This is when he uses that very particular word presumptuous and repeats it three times.
sentences.zh: 这时他用了那个非常特别的词“傲慢”，并重复了三次。

sentences.en: The black soldier is so presumptuous.
sentences.zh: 黑人士兵太“傲慢”了。

sentences.en: What do you make of that word presumptuous?
sentences.zh: 你怎么看“傲慢”这个词？

sentences.en: It's such an interesting and cool word to use in this moment.
sentences.zh: 在这一刻用这个词真是太有趣、太酷了。

sentences.en: What does it strike you?
sentences.zh: 你有什么感觉？

sentences.en: It strikes me as he's looking at them and looking at the fact that these young armed men in uniform
sentences.zh: 我感觉他看着他们，看着这些身穿制服、手持武器的年轻人，

sentences.en: don't have to lower their eyes, they don't have to lower their heads.
sentences.zh: 他们不必低眉顺眼，不必低头。

sentences.en: They're not cowing to white people, right?
sentences.zh: 他们不再对白人卑躬屈膝，对吧？

sentences.en: Instead, they're here and they're like turning this whole world on fire, right?
sentences.zh: 相反，他们就在这里，就像要把整个世界点燃一样，对吧？

sentences.en: He likely saw them as destroying the institution of slavery.
sentences.zh: 他很可能认为他们是在摧毁奴隶制。

sentences.en: They're burning it down and in burning it down, they are setting us free.
sentences.zh: 他们正在烧毁它，而在烧毁它的过程中，他们正在让我们获得自由。

sentences.en: In the meantime, Harriet Tubman is, as ever, on the front lines.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，哈丽特·塔布曼一如既往地在前线。

sentences.en: We know that Tubman got out on a rowboat and went to a plantation and she went to the slave cabins.
sentences.zh: 我们知道塔布曼坐划艇去了一个种植园，并去了奴隶小屋。

sentences.en: And I've said that there were enslaved people working in the rice fields.
sentences.zh: 我说过有奴隶在稻田里劳作。

sentences.en: The able-bodied people, including 88-year-old Minas Hamilton and his wife,
sentences.zh: 那些有劳动能力的人，包括88岁的迈纳斯·汉密尔顿和他的妻子，

sentences.en: were working in the fields that early in the morning.
sentences.zh: 那天清晨都在田里干活。

sentences.en: So the people who were left in the cabins were extremely, even more elderly,
sentences.zh: 所以留在小屋里的人，年纪更大，

sentences.en: but infirm, disabled children who were too young to work.
sentences.zh: 或者体弱多病、残疾，还有太小不能干活的孩子。

sentences.en: Women who had recently given birth or had very young nursing infants.
sentences.zh: 刚生完孩子或有年幼哺乳婴儿的妇女。

sentences.en: Those are the people who would have been left in the slave cabins.
sentences.zh: 这些人就是会被留在奴隶小屋里的人。

sentences.en: Tubman went to the cabins to get these most vulnerable people.
sentences.zh: 塔布曼去小屋是为了救这些最脆弱的人。

sentences.en: And she remembers this wonderful image of running with the freedom seekers,
sentences.zh: 她记得那个美妙的画面，和寻求自由的人们一起奔跑，

sentences.en: running with them back to the boats.
sentences.zh: 和他们一起跑回船上。

sentences.en: So she's helping women carry their children and she's helping carry these two pigs,
sentences.zh: 她帮妇女抱着孩子，还帮着带这两头猪，

sentences.en: which they named after Confederate officers and which were going to be given to the Union commanders,
sentences.zh: 它们是以邦联军官的名字命名的，本来是要送给联邦指挥官的，

sentences.en: the Union generals back in Buford.
sentences.zh: 也就是博福特的联邦将军们。

sentences.en: And she talks about one woman who's running.
sentences.zh: 她还提到一个正在奔跑的妇女。

sentences.en: She's got, you know, children in her arms and children holding on to her skirt
sentences.zh: 她怀里抱着孩子，裙子上还挂着孩子，

sentences.en: and one child on her shoulders and she's got a rice pot on her head.
sentences.zh: 肩上扛着一个孩子，头上顶着一个饭锅。

sentences.en: And the pot is smoking.
sentences.zh: 锅还在冒烟。

sentences.en: They pulled it off the fire.
sentences.zh: 他们刚从火上取下来。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: And the child is eating in flight.
sentences.zh: 孩子还在逃难途中吃着饭。

sentences.en: It's a wonderful image.
sentences.zh: 这画面太美好了。

sentences.en: And Tubman runs through some of these like thorn bushes near the edge of the rice field and she tears her skirt.
sentences.zh: 塔布曼跑过稻田边缘的一些荆棘丛，把裙子撕破了。

sentences.en: And so she laments the fact that she nearly tore her skirt off and writes a letter or has someone write a letter for her to the women of Boston,
sentences.zh: 她感叹自己差点把裙子撕烂，并写了一封信，或者让人代写了一封信给波士顿的妇女们，

sentences.en: asking them to send her a pair of bloomers and telling them that she'll probably need them for another expedition.
sentences.zh: 请求她们寄给她一条灯笼裤，并告诉她们她可能下一次远征还需要穿。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: It's amazing.
sentences.zh: 太神奇了。

sentences.en: She learned she just wasn't dressed for the job.
sentences.zh: 她意识到自己的穿着不适合这项工作。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: She's going in there to rescue the babies.
sentences.zh: 她去那里是为了营救孩子们。

sentences.en: She needs pants on.
sentences.zh: 她需要穿裤子。

sentences.en: She needs pants.
sentences.zh: 她需要裤子。

sentences.en: Yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: Plantations are burning.
sentences.zh: 种植园在燃烧。

sentences.en: Freedom seekers are being rowed to the boats.
sentences.zh: 寻求自由的人们正被划艇送往船上。

sentences.en: But this is, after all, a secret raid.
sentences.zh: 但毕竟，这是一次秘密突袭。

sentences.en: And the raiders only have so much time.
sentences.zh: 突袭者的时间非常有限。

sentences.en: On one plantation, the slave owners started to fight back.
sentences.zh: 在一个种植园里，奴隶主开始反击。

sentences.en: The overseer was able to get some of the Confederate soldiers to follow him back to the plantation.
sentences.zh: 监工成功带回了一些邦联士兵跟随他回到种植园。

sentences.en: And they positioned themselves between the freedom seekers and the boat, which stopped many people from actually getting to freedom.
sentences.zh: 他们挡在寻求自由者和船只之间，这阻止了许多人真正获得自由。

sentences.en: And one enslaved girl ran for it and she was shot and killed in cold blood.
sentences.zh: 有一个奴隶女孩试图逃跑，结果被冷血枪杀。

sentences.en: The raiders are out of time.
sentences.zh: 突袭者的时间到了。

sentences.en: And as freedom seekers realized this, some become desperate, trying to get on the last departing rowboats.
sentences.zh: 当寻求自由的人们意识到这一点时，有些人变得绝望，试图挤上最后一批离开的划艇。

sentences.en: There were descriptions of them holding on to the sides of the rowboats and trying to stop the rowboats from leaving without them.
sentences.zh: 有描述称，他们紧紧抓住划艇的边缘，试图阻止划艇在没有他们的情况下离开。

sentences.en: And at one point, Colonel Montgomery tells Harriet Tubman to sing to your people, right?
sentences.zh: 而且在某个时刻，蒙哥马利上校告诉哈丽特·塔布曼要为她的人民唱歌，对吧？

sentences.en: To calm them, sing to them.
sentences.zh: 为了安抚他们，给他们唱歌。

sentences.en: And she does.
sentences.zh: 她照做了。

sentences.en: And they become calm and kind of let go of the sides of the rowboat.
sentences.zh: 他们平静了下来，松开了划艇的边缘。

sentences.en: And the boat takes off without them.
sentences.zh: 船在没有他们的情况下出发了。

sentences.en: So we can only imagine what happened to those people, that they were tortured.
sentences.zh: 所以我们只能想象那些人遭遇了什么，他们遭到了折磨。

sentences.en: Some of them may have been killed for trying to escape.
sentences.zh: 他们中有些人可能因为试图逃跑而被杀害。

sentences.en: Some of them may have been sold for trying to escape.
sentences.zh: 有些人可能因为试图逃跑而被卖掉。

sentences.en: So 756 people get onto the boats and the boats sail all night and arrive early in the morning back in downtown Beaufort, back at the dock.
sentences.zh: 最终有756人登上了船，船只航行了一整夜，于清晨回到了博福特市中心，回到了码头。

sentences.en: Beaufort, the oasis of freedom, now home to 10,000 formerly enslaved people living free.
sentences.zh: 博福特，这片自由的绿洲，如今成了10,000名曾经被奴役的人自由生活的地方。

sentences.en: And on that morning that the Cumbie Freedom Seekers arrived back in Beaufort, people came out.
sentences.zh: 在康比自由寻求者回到博福特的那天早上，人们都出来了。

sentences.en: People came out to see them and line the streets.
sentences.zh: 人们出来看他们，挤满了街道。

sentences.en: And many of these people had been free for a year, years, since November 1861.
sentences.zh: 这些人中许多人自1861年11月以来已经自由了一年，甚至更久。

sentences.en: They had jobs, they had houses, they had food and clothing, and their kids were in school.
sentences.zh: 他们有工作、有房子、有食物和衣服，孩子们也在上学。

sentences.en: They had left slavery behind.
sentences.zh: 他们已经把奴隶制抛在了身后。

sentences.en: And yet here were 756 people who were straight out of the rice fields, right?
sentences.zh: 然而，这里有756人是刚从稻田里出来的，对吧？

sentences.en: In the same dirty gray field clothes, as the newspapers describe them, that they wore to their forced labor at four o'clock in the morning.
sentences.zh: 正如报纸所描述的那样，他们穿着和凌晨四点被迫劳动时一样的脏灰色田间工作服。

sentences.en: And the newspaper accounts talk about just their bodies, right?
sentences.zh: 报纸的报道谈到了他们的身体状况，对吧？

sentences.en: Skin and bones, lots of injuries.
sentences.zh: 皮包骨头，伤痕累累。

sentences.en: People just looked sick and emaciated and broken down and nearly naked, right?
sentences.zh: 人们看起来病恹恹的，骨瘦如柴，身体垮掉，几乎赤身裸体，对吧？

sentences.en: They're in horrible shape, physical shape.
sentences.zh: 他们的身体状况非常糟糕。

sentences.en: But it also talks about how they're beaming with pride.
sentences.zh: 但报道也谈到了他们脸上洋溢的自豪感。

sentences.en: As they parade down the main street in Beaufort, they are beaming with pride because they are finally free.
sentences.zh: 当他们在博福特的主街上游行时，他们脸上洋溢着自豪，因为他们终于自由了。

sentences.en: And they are finally able to reunite their families.
sentences.zh: 他们终于能够让家人团聚了。

sentences.en: Minus Hamilton is there, walking down the main street with his feisty wife, Hagar.
sentences.zh: 迈纳斯·汉密尔顿在那里，和他的悍妻哈加尔走在主街上。

sentences.en: So is their grown-up daughter, Bina Mack.
sentences.zh: 还有他们成年的女儿比娜·麦克。

sentences.en: She made it onto the boat too, along with her husband, Harry, and their little daughter, also named Hagar.
sentences.zh: 她也登上了船，和她的丈夫哈里以及他们的小女儿（也叫哈加尔）在一起。

sentences.en: Tyra Brown Polite and Phoebe Frazier found one another among the freedom seekers.
sentences.zh: 泰拉·布朗·波利特和菲比·弗雷泽在自由寻求者中找到了彼此。

sentences.en: The friends had been separated, sold to different plantations along the Combi.
sentences.zh: 这两位朋友曾被分开，卖到了康比沿岸不同的种植园。

sentences.en: But both made it onto the boat that day.
sentences.zh: 但那天她们都登上了船。

sentences.en: There's an elderly couple named November and Sarah Small Osborne, childhood sweethearts, who finally made it to freedom together.
sentences.zh: 还有一对叫诺文伯和莎拉·斯莫尔·奥斯本的老夫妇，他们是青梅竹马，最终一起获得了自由。

sentences.en: There's a seven-year-old girl named Martha Singleton.
sentences.zh: 还有一个叫玛莎·辛格尔顿的七岁女孩。

sentences.en: And Andrew and Diana Harris still grieving for their four small children who died back on the plantation.
sentences.zh: 安德鲁和戴安娜·哈里斯仍在为他们死在种植园的四个年幼的孩子哀悼。

sentences.en: But they made it to Beaufort that day with their only surviving child, a little boy named Samuel.
sentences.zh: 但那天他们带着唯一的幸存者，一个小男孩塞缪尔，成功抵达了博福特。

sentences.en: I mean, how do you feel when you think about that scene?
sentences.zh: 我是说，当你想到那个场景时，你有什么感觉？

sentences.en: It brings tears to my eyes.
sentences.zh: 这让我热泪盈眶。

sentences.en: It does to me too.
sentences.zh: 我也是。

sentences.en: It really does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It really, really does.
sentences.zh: 真的，真的如此。

sentences.en: Think about what the Combi Freedom Seekers' lives were like in these ghastly death camps, labor-slash-death camps of these rice plantations.
sentences.zh: 想想康比自由寻求者在那些可怕的死亡营，那些稻田种植园的劳动兼死亡营里的生活是什么样的。

sentences.en: By the time they're parading down Beaufort, they finally made it.
sentences.zh: 当他们在博福特游行时，他们终于成功了。

sentences.en: They're finally free.
sentences.zh: 他们终于自由了。

sentences.en: That day, everyone gathers at a church in downtown Beaufort, including the leaders of the raid, Colonel James Montgomery and Harriet Tubman.
sentences.zh: 那天，每个人都聚集在博福特市中心的一座教堂里，包括突袭行动的领导人詹姆斯·蒙哥马利上校和哈丽特·塔布曼。

sentences.en: Colonel James Montgomery gives a speech to the Freedom Seekers, and Harriet Tubman follows him.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·蒙哥马利上校向自由寻求者发表了演讲，哈丽特·塔布曼紧随其后。

sentences.en: And we don't know what she said.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道她说了什么。

sentences.en: There's no transcript.
sentences.zh: 没有文字记录。

sentences.en: And it's not on YouTube, but...
sentences.zh: YouTube上也没有，但是……

sentences.en: Oh, if only.
sentences.zh: 噢，要是能听到就好了。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: Your life would be so much easier.
sentences.zh: 你的生活会轻松得多。

sentences.en: So much easier.
sentences.zh: 轻松得多。

sentences.en: I can't even imagine.
sentences.zh: 我简直无法想象。

sentences.en: But, you know, it's after her speech that 150 men aged 14 to 70, there was one 70-year-old man who enlisted.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，是在她演讲之后，150名14到70岁的男子应征入伍，其中还有一位70岁的老人。

sentences.en: The morning after they're liberated, they enlist in the second South Carolina Volunteers.
sentences.zh: 在他们获得解放的第二天早上，他们加入了南卡罗来纳第二志愿军。

sentences.en: It was a very immediate kind of thing, that they came and liberated us.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常直接的反应，他们来解放了我们。

sentences.en: We are going to liberate others.
sentences.zh: 我们要去解放其他人。

sentences.en: And that brings us back to the pension files, where we began this story.
sentences.zh: 这让我们回到了养老金档案，也就是我们故事开始的地方。

sentences.en: Our object that in many ways holds the stories of this raid.
sentences.zh: 我们的物品在许多方面承载了这次突袭的故事。

sentences.en: About 200,000 black men served during the Civil War.
sentences.zh: 内战期间约有20万黑人服役。

sentences.en: And after the war is over, those men, their widows, their dependent children, were entitled to military pensions, just like veterans today.
sentences.zh: 战争结束后，这些人、他们的遗孀和受抚养的子女都有权获得军事养老金，就像今天的退伍军人一样。

sentences.en: And that application process was long and laborious, and it required a lot of paperwork.
sentences.zh: 申请过程漫长而艰辛，需要大量的文书工作。

sentences.en: It didn't matter if you were a black soldier or a white soldier.
sentences.zh: 无论你是黑人士兵还是白人士兵，这都不重要。

sentences.en: You had to provide proof that you were who you said you were and that you had served.
sentences.zh: 你必须提供证明，证明你是你所说的那个人，并且你确实服过役。

sentences.en: But the difference is that the black veterans and the widows were born enslaved, so they didn't have any paperwork, right?
sentences.zh: 但不同之处在于，黑人退伍军人和遗孀是作为奴隶出生的，所以他们没有任何文书，对吧？

sentences.en: They didn't have birth certificates, marriage certificates, death certificates.
sentences.zh: 他们没有出生证明、结婚证明、死亡证明。

sentences.en: What the veterans had is they had people, people they grew up with, and the men they joined the military with, and the women they married, right?
sentences.zh: 退伍军人拥有的是人，他们一起长大的人，一起参军的战友，以及他们娶的妻子，对吧？

sentences.en: And these people came out and testified for each other.
sentences.zh: 这些人站出来为彼此作证。

sentences.en: And it's through their testimony that they verify each other's identity, the sanctity of their marriages, the legitimacy of their children.
sentences.zh: 正是通过他们的证词，他们验证了彼此的身份、婚姻的神圣性以及子女的合法性。

sentences.en: Who held them in bondage and where?
sentences.zh: 谁在什么地方奴役了他们？

sentences.en: And how they were bought, mortgaged, given away, and passed down within families.
sentences.zh: 他们是如何被买卖、抵押、赠送以及在家族内传承的。

sentences.en: And then they talk about their lives together, courting.
sentences.zh: 然后他们谈论他们在一起的生活，谈恋爱。

sentences.en: They go through the veterans and the widows' entire dating history.
sentences.zh: 他们回顾了退伍军人和遗孀的整个恋爱史。

sentences.en: Because they have to show that they're actually legally married to this person, right?
sentences.zh: 因为他们必须证明他们确实与此人合法结婚，对吧？

sentences.en: And they're not married to those other people.
sentences.zh: 而且他们没有和那些其他人结婚。

sentences.en: You see the whole life of people in the enslaved community in ways that we've never seen them before,
sentences.zh: 你以我们从未见过的方式看到了奴隶社区人们的完整生活，

sentences.en: because now they're telling their story.
sentences.zh: 因为现在他们在讲述自己的故事。

sentences.en: Once you know that these files exist and you see them in all the oral history that they create,
sentences.zh: 一旦你知道这些档案存在，并且看到它们创造的所有口述历史，

sentences.en: what do you realize you can do with these files when it comes to the raid?
sentences.zh: 你意识到在突袭事件中你可以用这些档案做什么？

sentences.en: I realize that I can put the enslaved community back together.
sentences.zh: 我意识到我可以把奴隶社区重新拼凑起来。

sentences.en: I realize that I can identify the people who were liberated in the raid.
sentences.zh: 我意识到我可以识别出在突袭中被解放的人。

sentences.en: Those people who testified about the raid become the main characters of the story.
sentences.zh: 那些为突袭作证的人成为了故事的主角。

sentences.en: The pension files also helped Etta rebuild her own family tree,
sentences.zh: 养老金档案也帮助埃塔重建了她自己的家谱，

sentences.en: because Etta's family hails from a county not far from Beaufort.
sentences.zh: 因为埃塔的家族来自离博福特不远的一个县。

sentences.en: But she didn't have much to go on, just a little research her cousin had done.
sentences.zh: 但她没有太多线索，只有她表亲做的一点研究。

sentences.en: When I started looking for the Fields family, I went back to the notes my cousin gave me,
sentences.zh: 当我开始寻找菲尔兹家族时，我翻看了表亲给我的笔记，

sentences.en: and I saw that he had searched through the census
sentences.zh: 我看到他在人口普查中进行了搜索，

sentences.en: and identified our earliest known ancestor in the 1870 census as Hector Fields.
sentences.zh: 并在1870年的人口普查中确定了我们已知最早的祖先是赫克托·菲尔兹。

sentences.en: But then he was stuck.
sentences.zh: 但随后他就卡住了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That's as far back as he could go.
sentences.zh: 那是他能追溯到的最远记录。

sentences.en: So the census said that Etta had a great-great-great-grandfather named Hector.
sentences.zh: 所以人口普查显示埃塔有一位名叫赫克托的曾曾曾祖父。

sentences.en: But that was kind of it.
sentences.zh: 但也就仅此而已了。

sentences.en: It's a dead end that people frequently hit when looking for ancestors who were enslaved.
sentences.zh: 这是人们在寻找被奴役的祖先时经常遇到的死胡同。

sentences.en: The 1870 census was the first government document that listed formerly enslaved people
sentences.zh: 1870年的人口普查是第一份列出曾经被奴役的人的政府文件，

sentences.en: by first and last name, which makes it really hard to trace anyone further back than that.
sentences.zh: 上面有名字和姓氏，这使得在此之前追溯任何人变得非常困难。

sentences.en: In fact, people call it the 1870 brick wall.
sentences.zh: 事实上，人们称之为1870年的砖墙。

sentences.en: A brick wall that Etta herself was facing.
sentences.zh: 埃塔自己也面临着这堵砖墙。

sentences.en: So how do you find Hector Fields?
sentences.zh: 那么你如何找到赫克托·菲尔兹呢？

sentences.en: I was working with the International African-American Museum Center for Family History.
sentences.zh: 我当时在国际非裔美国人博物馆家庭历史中心工作。

sentences.en: They identified Hector Fields as a veteran in Beaufort.
sentences.zh: 他们确定赫克托·菲尔兹是博福特的一名退伍军人。

sentences.en: So I took these little lists, and I went down to the National Archives,
sentences.zh: 所以我拿着这些小名单，去了国家档案馆，

sentences.en: and I pulled these pension files.
sentences.zh: 调出了这些养老金档案。

sentences.en: And Hector's file was a buSt.
sentences.zh: 赫克托的档案一无所获。

sentences.en: There was no family information.
sentences.zh: 里面没有家庭信息。

sentences.en: It was like 30 pages long.
sentences.zh: 它大约有30页长。

sentences.en: I put it on the shelf.
sentences.zh: 我把它放回了架子上。

sentences.en: You know, when I looked at the other pension files, the beauty came when we discovered the
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我查看其他养老金档案时，真正的惊喜来自于我们发现了

sentences.en: pension file of Hector's brother, Jonas Fields.
sentences.zh: 赫克托的兄弟乔纳斯·菲尔兹的养老金档案。

sentences.en: This pension file, the file from Hector's brother, was more than 250 pages long.
sentences.zh: 这份养老金档案，也就是赫克托兄弟的档案，有250多页长。

sentences.en: And it contained precious details about the Fields family, details that Etta never would have
sentences.zh: 它包含了关于菲尔兹家族的珍贵细节，这些细节是埃塔永远无法

sentences.en: learned otherwise.
sentences.zh: 通过其他方式了解到的。

sentences.en: The name of his siblings, the names of their parents, how they got separated during the war.
sentences.zh: 他兄弟姐妹的名字，他们父母的名字，他们在战争中是如何失散的。

sentences.en: My aunt was given away as a wedding gift.
sentences.zh: 我的姑姑被当作结婚礼物送人了。

sentences.en: The slaveholder gave her to his daughter when she got married.
sentences.zh: 奴隶主在她结婚时把她送给了自己的女儿。

sentences.en: So the whole, it just opened up so many doors for our family history.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切，它为我们的家族史打开了许多扇门。

sentences.en: Etta followed one document to another, one pension file to the next, until she learned something
sentences.zh: 埃塔顺着一份文件找到另一份，从一份养老金档案查到下一份，直到她了解到

sentences.en: that no one in her family had known before.
sentences.zh: 她家族中从未有人知道的事情。

sentences.en: That Hector Fields, her great-great-great-grandfather, was one of the soldiers on the Comby raid.
sentences.zh: 赫克托·菲尔兹，她的曾曾曾祖父，是康比突袭行动中的士兵之一。

sentences.en: That he took part in freeing 756 people from bondage.
sentences.zh: 他参与了解放756人脱离奴役的行动。

sentences.en: Her own ancestor was among those presumptuous black soldiers who set the world on fire.
sentences.zh: 她自己的祖先就在那些让世界为之震颤的傲慢黑人士兵之中。

sentences.en: Of all the remarkable things that Etta was able to do with these pension files, there's one that stands apart.
sentences.zh: 在埃塔利用这些养老金档案所做的所有非凡事情中，有一件事脱颖而出。

sentences.en: Not because it's the most complex, but because it may be the most basic.
sentences.zh: 不是因为它最复杂，而是因为它可能是最基础的。

sentences.en: She was able to restore people's real names.
sentences.zh: 她能够恢复人们的真实姓名。

sentences.en: The names of the soldiers and the freedom seekers who took part in the raid.
sentences.zh: 参与突袭的士兵和自由寻求者的名字。

sentences.en: Not the names of their slaveholders, but the names they gave themselves.
sentences.zh: 不是奴隶主给他们的名字，而是他们自己取的名字。

sentences.en: Jack Aiken, Sunday Briscoe, Robert and Phoebe Frazier, Captain Brown, Edward and Peggy Brown.
sentences.zh: 杰克·艾肯、桑迪·布里斯科、罗伯特和菲比·弗雷泽、布朗上尉、爱德华和佩吉·布朗。

sentences.en: My goal was to tell the story of the notable and the nameless, right?
sentences.zh: 我的目标是讲述那些著名人物和无名之辈的故事，对吧？

sentences.en: The people we know and the people we don't know.
sentences.zh: 我们认识的人和我们不认识的人。

sentences.en: The people whose names we know and the people whose names we've never heard before.
sentences.zh: 我们知道名字的人和我们从未听说过名字的人。

sentences.en: And their names have never been recorded before.
sentences.zh: 他们的名字以前从未被记录过。

sentences.en: Cuffy and Sophia Bowles.
sentences.zh: 卡菲和索菲亚·鲍尔斯。

sentences.en: Samson Drayton.
sentences.zh: 萨姆森·德雷顿。

sentences.en: Thomas and Bella Drayton.
sentences.zh: 托马斯和贝拉·德雷顿。

sentences.en: And so how do we identify their names and tell their stories and then write their names in the annals of history?
sentences.zh: 那么我们如何确定他们的名字，讲述他们的故事，然后将他们的名字写入历史的史册呢？

sentences.en: That's what I wanted to do.
sentences.zh: 这就是我想做的事情。

sentences.en: Carolina, Flora and Stephanie Grant.
sentences.zh: 卡罗琳娜、弗洛拉和斯蒂芬妮·格兰特。

sentences.en: Jackson and Jane Grant.
sentences.zh: 杰克逊和简·格兰特。

sentences.en: Jeffrey and Phoebe Gray.
sentences.zh: 杰弗里和菲比·格雷。

sentences.en: Dr. Etta Fields Black, thank you so much for talking with me.
sentences.zh: 埃塔·菲尔兹·布莱克博士，非常感谢您与我交谈。

sentences.en: I really enjoyed it.
sentences.zh: 我真的很享受。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you for inviting me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢您的邀请。
